correctness.rationale: For each m,n>=5, the Alexander dual has exactly all vertices/pairs, 6mn induced two-edge path triangles and mn coordinate-square tetrahedra, with no larger faces (edge-triple incidence divisibility excludes five-sets). Two explicit free-face removals per square and two per vertex for straight paths leave a triangulated torus and C(mn,2)-6mn loose loop edges, a complete integral simple-homotopy derivation. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality gives Z in degree mn-5 and \(\mathbb Z^{\binom{mn}{2}-6mn+2}\) in degree mn-4; all others zero. The standalone checker independently enumerated faces, verified free pairs and F2 boundary ranks for (5,5),(5,6),(6,6). It does not substitute for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Eight actual semantic research-record queries plus full-text inspection of the most relevant primary sources identify no earlier ordinary three-cut integral homology classification for C_m Cartesian C_n, m,n>=5. The closest same-object results instead treat rectangular path grids, single squared cycles, or distinct complexes on toroidal grids. A general Euler identity is weaker than the two integral groups and constructive torus collapse. Search is not an exhaustive priority certificate.

value.rationale: The rectangular grid three-cut complexes are shellable, so toroidal boundary identification poses a natural structural gap. The dual retains a genuine two-dimensional torus fundamental class rather than only a wedge of circles or spheres, forcing next-to-top integral homology and persistent non-shellability throughout a two-parameter periodic graph family. Both exact integral ranks are determined; neither follows from earlier rectangular-grid Betti counts or general Euler formulas. The claim is an all-order structural classification with a clear topological mechanism, not an arbitrary finite graph count.
